origin: Our sources describe Italian as a whole rather than its earliest stage. Modern Italian is a standardised form of literary Florentine Tuscan, and together with Sardinian it is the least differentiated language from Latin. That closeness to Latin is why Italian is called a conservative Romance language, and it is a useful clue to what its earlier stages may have sounded like.
